draft_notes: Two new BEHAVIOR source tasks are proposed: one selected bowl transferred from a dining booth to a kitchen sink from putting_dirty_dishes_in_sink-0; and one selected plate cleaned of source-listed breadcrumb and pesto residues from washing_plates-0. Both are primitive task proposals, but the latter's Atlas skill_wipe mapping and concrete procedure remain design proposals because the source describes symbolic states/resources rather than robot motion.

Atlas hierarchy paths: task_reference_behavior_bowl_to_sink_round2 --acts_on--> behavior_object_bowl_byzaxy --instance_of--> concept:object_dish; task_reference_behavior_clean_plate_round2 --acts_on--> behavior_object_plate_aewthq --instance_of--> concept:object_dish. Each path has exactly two hierarchy edges, both ObjectInstances are distinct, and the shared ObjectClass is a curator grouping only.

Source taxonomies remain separate: bowl-byzaxy is category bowl / bowl.n.01, whose parent is vessel.n.03; plate-aewthq is category plate / plate.n.04, whose parent is flatware.n.01. None of these source synsets is asserted equivalent to Atlas object_dish.

The BEHAVIOR source task pages scope object roles to synsets, not the specific model IDs selected here. The model pages/catalog entries support identity and BEHAVIOR readiness only; compatibility remains unknown. All missing booth, sink, scrub-brush, water, soap, bathroom-floor, and countertop assets are unresolved plan requirements, not fabricated object records. Population frequency, robot execution, compatibility, and all time estimates remain unknown/null.
